entities.description: Composer, pianist, and choir director; the central organizing figure of Chicago gospel's institutional network in the 1930s.
entities.name: Thomas A. Dorsey

entities.description: Gospel singer; migrated to Chicago in 1927 and credited the city's organizational/business environment with opening possibilities.
entities.name: Mahalia Jackson

entities.description: Gospel pioneer; pianist for Ebenezer's Young People's Choir; organized the Martin-Frye Quartet (1933), renamed the Roberta Martin Singers (1936).
entities.name: Roberta Martin

entities.description: Gospel entrepreneur; introduced Dorsey's music in Chicago-area Black churches, managed finances and markets; co-founded Dorsey House of Music (1932) and Martin & Morris Music Co. (1940).
entities.name: Sallie Martin

entities.description: Arranger, transcriber, and publisher; arranged at Bowles' House of Music; organist at First Church of Deliverance; recommended the 1939 Hammond organ; co-founded Martin & Morris Music Co. (1940).
entities.name: Kenneth Morris

entities.description: Choir director; directed the Ebenezer gospel chorus (debut Jan. 1932) with Dorsey at piano; co-namesake of the Martin-Frye Quartet (1933).
entities.name: Theodore Frye

entities.description: Pastor of Ebenezer Missionary Baptist Church; called for a gospel chorus on December 6, 1931.
entities.name: Rev. James Smith

entities.description: Pastor of Pilgrim Baptist Church; hired Thomas A. Dorsey in 1931/32 to organize a gospel chorus.
entities.name: Rev. Junius C. Austin

entities.description: Pastor of First Church of Deliverance; launched its 1935 radio broadcast; installed Kenneth Morris; provided financial help to launch Martin & Morris Music Co.
entities.name: Rev. Clarence H. Cobbs

entities.description: Gospel singer/composer; sang in Pilgrim's childhood choir; later associated with Dorsey's mentorship network.
entities.name: James Cleveland
entities.notes: Inherited from sibling CTL-DR-MUSIC-001; mentorship edge not independently re-verified in this pass.

entities.description: Gospel singer; among those who sang at Pilgrim Baptist Church (per NMAAHC object record); member of the Caravans.
entities.name: Albertina Walker

entities.description: Bronzeville Baptist church in the 1890–91 Adler and Sullivan building; housed the Pilgrim congregation since 1922; Dorsey's music-director base from the early 1930s; gutted by fire Jan. 6, 2006.
entities.name: Pilgrim Baptist Church

entities.description: Bronzeville Baptist church; site of the Dec. 1931 gospel-chorus call and Jan. 1932 ~100-member chorus debut; calls itself home of the first modern gospel choir (self-claim, disputed).
entities.name: Ebenezer Missionary Baptist Church

entities.description: Bronzeville church under Rev. Clarence H. Cobbs; launched a 1935 radio broadcast and acquired an early Hammond organ in 1939.
entities.name: First Church of Deliverance

entities.description: Chicago church whose W. D. Cook choir participated in the pivotal 1932 convocation with Ebenezer and Pilgrim (per Harris).
entities.name: Metropolitan Community Church
entities.notes: Named via Harris's 1932 convocation account; not independently verified in this pass.

entities.description: National gospel convention co-founded by Dorsey and associates; founding date disputed (1932 vs 1933).
entities.name: National Convention of Gospel Choirs and Choruses

entities.description: Sheet-music publishing house launched 1932 with Sallie Martin's help.
entities.name: Dorsey House of Music

entities.description: Music house where Kenneth Morris arranged and transcribed songs before joining First Church of Deliverance.
entities.name: Bowles' House of Music
entities.notes: A pre-existing publishing node; avenue for follow-up research.

entities.description: Gospel sheet-music publisher founded 1940 by Sallie Martin and Kenneth Morris; catalog carried hundreds of songs; distributed nationally.
entities.name: Martin & Morris Music Company

entities.description: Chicago record label with a substantial gospel catalog (Staple Singers, Caravans, Swan Silvertones); later expansion/distribution node.
entities.name: Vee-Jay Records

entities.description: Touring gospel ensemble founded by Roberta Martin (as Martin-Frye Quartet, 1933; renamed 1936); women joined mid-1940s.
entities.name: Roberta Martin Singers

entities.description: Chicago gospel group (Albertina Walker among members); recorded by Vee-Jay; part of the later expansion generation.
entities.name: The Caravans
entities.notes: Inherited from sibling; Vee-Jay recording role standard but not independently re-verified here.

entities.description: Gospel group; relocated to Chicago as part of the Great Migration; 1956 Vee-Jay gospel hit 'Uncloudy Day.'
entities.name: The Staple Singers

entities.description: Smithsonian museum holding Dorsey's Pilgrim rehearsal piano (2015.134.1a-g) and gospel archival material.
entities.name: National Museum of African American History and Culture

entities.description: Planned museum on the Pilgrim Baptist site at 3301 S. Indiana Ave.; announced Dec. 2017; $2.1M state grant (June 2022); $10M first-phase estimate.
entities.name: National Museum of Gospel Music (planned)

entities.description: 1930s Conover (Cable Piano Co., Chicago) baby grand used by Thomas A. Dorsey as rehearsal piano at Pilgrim Baptist Church; rights: No Known Copyright Restrictions.
entities.name: Conover baby grand rehearsal piano (NMAAHC 2015.134.1a-g)

entities.description: Fire that gutted Pilgrim Baptist Church, destroying decades of records and likely/reportably original Dorsey sheet music.
entities.name: Pilgrim Baptist Church fire, January 6, 2006

entities.description: Pivotal 1932 convocation involving Ebenezer, Pilgrim, and Metropolitan's W. D. Cook choir (per Harris); candidate precursor to the NCGCC.
entities.name: 1932 gospel convocation (Ebenezer / Pilgrim / Metropolitan)
entities.notes: Provisional reconciliation for the 1932/1933 founding-date conflict.

entities.description: Electric organ acquired by First Church of Deliverance in 1939 on Kenneth Morris's recommendation; its broadcast sound spread among churches.
entities.name: Hammond organ (instrument technology)

entities.description: Radio broadcast launched by Rev. Clarence H. Cobbs in 1935; exposed listeners to the church's sound and drew audiences.
entities.name: First Church of Deliverance radio broadcast (1935)
entities.notes: Station call letters not verified in this pass.

title: Why Chicago Became a Gospel Center — Entities
